theme.title: The Promise Kept
theme.summary: From Eden to Bethlehem: one step of the promise each day, what God said, how the Church reads it, until on Christmas Eve the promise has a name.

topics.name: Advent
topics.summary: The season as a whole: what Advent is, its signs, its saints and its call to watch.

topics.name: Advent Challenge
topics.summary: One step of the promise each day, from Eden to Bethlehem.

levels.title: Two Comings, One Watch
levels.reflection: Advent looks two ways at once. When the Church keeps it each year, she makes present the ancient expectancy of the Messiah, sharing in the long preparation for the Savior's first coming, and so the faithful renew their ardent desire for his second coming. We wait like people who know the Master is certain to come but not when. That is why the Lord says, "Watch." Over the next four weeks you will walk the road the prophets walked, one step of the promise each day, until on Christmas Eve the promise has a name.

scripture.text: Watch ye therefore, because ye know not what hour your Lord will come.

levels.title: The First Promise
levels.reflection: After the fall, man was not abandoned. In the book of Genesis God speaks to the serpent of enmity between it and the woman, and of her seed crushing its head. The Church calls this the Protoevangelium, the "first gospel": the first announcement of the Messiah and Redeemer, and of a final victory of a descendant of the woman. Christian tradition sees in it the New Adam, who by his obedience makes amends for the disobedience of Adam, and many Fathers see in the woman Mary, the new Eve. The whole promise begins here, in the dark, with a word of hope.

scripture.text: I will put enmities between thee and the woman, and thy seed and her seed: she shall crush thy head, and thou shalt lie in wait for her heel.

saint.name: St. Irenaeus
saint.reference: Adversus haereses 3, 22, 4, as quoted in CCC 494
saint.text: The knot of Eve's disobedience was untied by Mary's obedience: what the virgin Eve bound through her disbelief, Mary loosened by her faith.

levels.title: Abraham: All the Nations
levels.reflection: God calls Abram out of his country, his kindred and his father's house, and makes him Abraham, "the father of a multitude of nations." The promise reaches past one family: in him all the nations of the earth shall be blessed. Abraham's faith is tested when he is asked to offer his son, and he answers that God will provide himself a victim. The Church sees in that answer the shadow of the Father who did not spare his own Son. Saint Paul says the scripture, foreseeing that God justifies the Gentiles by faith, told Abraham beforehand. The promise was never only for Israel.

scripture.text: I will bless them that bless thee, and curse them that curse thee, and IN THEE shall all the kindred of the earth be blessed:

levels.title: The Lamb and the Prophet
levels.reflection: At the first Passover the blood on the doors was a sign: the Lord saw the blood and passed over. Centuries later John the Baptist points at Jesus and says, "Behold the Lamb of God, who taketh away the sin of the world." He is at once the suffering Servant and the Paschal Lamb, the symbol of Israel's redemption. Moses had also promised a prophet like himself, whom the people must hear, and Saint Peter says that prophet is Christ. At the Last Supper Jesus gave the Passover its definitive meaning, and the Eucharist fulfills it. Two promises, one answer.

scripture.text: The next day, John saw Jesus coming to him, and he saith: Behold the Lamb of God, behold him who taketh away the sin of the world.

levels.title: A Star and a Scepter
levels.reflection: An oracle in the book of Numbers looks far ahead to a figure not yet near: "A star shall rise out of Jacob and a sceptre shall spring up from Israel." Jacob had said the scepter would not be taken away from Judah until he comes who is to be sent, "the expectation of nations." The wise men follow a star to ask where the king of the Jews is born, and the Book of Revelation names him: the lion of the tribe of Judah, the root of David. The Church sees in the Magi the first-fruits of the nations. The promise made to one tribe was always meant for the whole world.

scripture.text: I shall see him, but not now: I shall behold him, but not near. A STAR SHALL RISE out of Jacob and a sceptre shall spring up from Israel: and shall strike the chiefs of Moab, and shall waste all the children of Seth.

saint.name: St. Leo the Great
saint.reference: Sermo 3 in epiphania Domini, as quoted in CCC 528
saint.text: The Epiphany shows that "the full number of the nations" now takes its "place in the family of the patriarchs", and acquires Israelitica dignitas (is made "worthy of the heritage of Israel").

levels.title: The Throne Forever
levels.reflection: God promises David a seed whose kingdom he will establish and whose throne he will establish for ever: "I will be to him a father, and he shall be to me a son." The book of Ruth traces the line backward from David: a son is born to Naomi, called Obed, "the father of Isai, the father of David." Saint Peter says David knew that God had sworn to him that one of the fruit of his loins would sit upon his throne. When Gabriel speaks to Mary the words return: the Lord God shall give him the throne of David his father, and of his kingdom there shall be no end.

scripture.text: And when thy days shall be fulfilled, and thou shalt sleep with thy fathers, I will raise up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom. He shall build a house to my name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom for ever. I will be to him a father, and he shall be to me a son: and if he commit any iniquity, I will correct him with the rod of men, and with the stripes of the children of men.

levels.title: Where God Dwells
levels.reflection: When Solomon's Temple was finished the priests came out of the sanctuary and a cloud filled the house of the Lord, for the glory of the Lord had filled it. Yet Solomon himself asked, "Is it then to be thought that God should indeed dwell upon earth?" Heaven and the heavens of heavens cannot contain him. Saint John answers: "The Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us." Jesus speaks of the temple of his body. The Church teaches that he identified himself with the Temple as God's definitive dwelling-place among men. The question Solomon asked has an answer you can hold in your arms.

scripture.text: Is it then to be thought that God should indeed dwell upon earth? for if heaven, and the heavens of heavens cannot contain thee, how much less this house which I have built?

levels.title: Elijah Must Come
levels.reflection: On Mount Carmel fire from the Lord consumed the holocaust, and the people fell on their faces: "The Lord he is God." Elijah's very name, "The Lord is my God", foretells that cry. The last prophet of the Old Testament promises that God will send Elijah before the great and dreadful day of the Lord. The angel tells Zechariah that his son will go before the Lord "in the spirit and power of Elias." Jesus tells his disciples that Elijah is already come, and they understood he spoke of John the Baptist. The Church calls John the voice who prepares the way.

scripture.text: Behold I will send you Elias the prophet, before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord. And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers: lest I come, and strike the earth with anathema.

levels.title: The Virgin's Sign
levels.reflection: King Ahaz is afraid. In his day the kings of Aram and Israel have marched against Judah, and Ahaz has turned to the king of Assyria for help. Isaiah comes with a sign that Ahaz did not ask for: "Behold a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and his name shall be called Emmanuel." Saint Matthew sees it fulfilled when the angel speaks to Joseph, and he gives the meaning of the name: God with us. The Church confesses that Jesus was conceived by the Holy Spirit without human seed, and the Fathers saw in this the sign that it truly was the Son of God who came in a humanity like our own.

scripture.text: Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign. Behold a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and his name shall be called Emmanuel.

saint.name: St. Ignatius of Antioch
saint.reference: Letter to the Smyrnaeans, as quoted in CCC 496
saint.text: You are firmly convinced about our Lord, who is truly of the race of David according to the flesh, Son of God according to the will and power of God, truly born of a virgin

levels.title: A Child Is Born to Us
levels.reflection: Isaiah speaks to the northern lands first: "The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light." Saint Matthew says this was fulfilled when Jesus began to preach in Galilee of the Gentiles. And the prophet speaks of a child: "a child is born to us, and a son is given to us ... Wonderful, Counsellor, God the Mighty, the Prince of Peace." Out of the root of Jesse a rod comes forth, and the spirit of the Lord rests on him. The Church sees in these verses the characteristics of the awaited Messiah. The light always arrives in the places that felt most forgotten.

scripture.text: For a CHILD IS BORN to us, and a son is given to us, and the government is upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called, Wonderful, Counsellor, God the Mighty, the Father of the world to come, the Prince of Peace.

saint.name: St. Jerome
saint.reference: Commentary on Isaiah, prologue, as quoted in CCC 133
saint.text: Ignorance of the Scriptures is ignorance of Christ.

levels.title: The Servant Who Suffers
levels.reflection: Isaiah sees a servant who is wounded for our iniquities and bruised for our sins, and by whose bruises we are healed. He is led like a sheep to the slaughter and does not open his mouth. A man from Ethiopia is reading these very words when Philip meets him on the road and asks if he understands. The man asks of whom the prophet speaks, and Philip begins at this scripture and preaches Jesus. The Church teaches that Jesus himself explained his life and death in the light of the suffering Servant. Saint Peter adds that he bore our sins in his body upon the tree.

scripture.text: But he was wounded for our iniquities, he was bruised for our sins: the chastisement of our peace was upon him, and by his bruises we are healed.

levels.title: Comfort, My People
levels.reflection: Jerusalem has been broken. The prophets had warned that forgetting the Law ends in the Exile, which the Church calls the apparent failure of the promises but in truth the mysterious fidelity of the Savior God. Then Isaiah hears a command: "Be comforted, be comforted, my people." Jeremiah hears a promise of a new covenant, written not on stone but on the heart, and Ezekiel promises a new heart of flesh. At the Last Supper Jesus takes the chalice: "the new testament in my blood." The New Testament lies hidden in the Old, and the Old is unveiled in the New.

scripture.text: Be comforted, be comforted, my people, saith your God. Speak ye to the heart of Jerusalem, and call to her: for her evil is come to an end, her iniquity is forgiven: she hath received of the hand of the Lord double for all her sins. The voice of one crying in the desert: Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make straight in the wilderness the paths of our God. Every valley shall be exalted, and every mountain and hill shall be made low, and the crooked shall become straight, and the rough ways plain. And the glory of the Lord shall be revealed, and all flesh together shall see, that the mouth of the Lord hath spoken.

saint.name: St. Augustine
saint.reference: cf. Quaestiones in Heptateuchum 2, 73, as in CCC 129
saint.text: As an old saying put it, the New Testament lies hidden in the Old and the Old Testament is unveiled in the New.

levels.title: One Like a Son of Man
levels.reflection: In a vision of the night Daniel sees one like the son of man coming with the clouds of heaven to the Ancient of days. To him is given power, glory and a kingdom, and all peoples, tribes and tongues shall serve him: his power is everlasting and his kingdom shall not be destroyed. When the high priest asks whether he is the Christ, Jesus answers with this vision: you shall see the Son of man sitting on the right hand of the power of God, and coming with the clouds of heaven. The Church teaches that Christ's being seated at the Father's right hand is the fulfillment of Daniel's vision.

scripture.text: I beheld therefore in the vision of the night, and lo, one like the son of man came with the clouds of heaven, and he came even to the Ancient of days: and they presented him before him. And he gave him power, and glory, and a kingdom: and all peoples, tribes and tongues shall serve him: his power is an everlasting power that shall not be taken away: and his kingdom that shall not be destroyed.

levels.title: The Last Prophet, the Final Word
levels.reflection: Malachi is the last voice of the Old Testament prophets: "Behold I send my angel, and he shall prepare the way before my face. And presently the Lord, whom you seek, shall come to his temple." Saint Mark opens his Gospel with these words. The Letter to the Hebrews says that God, who spoke in times past to the fathers by the prophets, in these days hath spoken to us by his Son. The Church teaches that Christ is the Father's one, perfect and unsurpassable Word: in him he has said everything, and there will be no other word than this one. The long waiting ends in a Person.

scripture.text: God, who, at sundry times and in divers manners, spoke in times past to the fathers by the prophets, last of all, In these days hath spoken to us by his Son, whom he hath appointed heir of all things, by whom also he made the world.

saint.name: St. John of the Cross
saint.reference: commenting on Hebrews 1:1-2, as quoted in CCC 65
saint.text: In giving us his Son, his only Word (for he possesses no other), he spoke everything to us at once in this sole Word - and he has no more to say.

levels.title: The Faith That Would Not Bend
levels.reflection: In 164 BC the Maccabees recaptured Jerusalem, and the Church's Scriptures remember a time when faithfulness cost lives. In the second book of Maccabees a mother stands beside her seven sons and encourages them to die rather than abandon the law: "God made them out of nothing, and mankind also." The Catechism calls this faith in creation out of nothing "a truth full of promise and hope." The Maccabean martyrs also confessed that the King of the universe will raise them up to an everlasting renewal of life. Winter in Jerusalem brings the feast of the dedication, which John mentions.

scripture.text: I beseech thee, my son, look upon heaven and earth, and all that is in them: and consider that God made them out of nothing, and mankind also:

saint.name: The mother of the seven sons
saint.text: I do not know how you came into being in my womb. It was not I who gave you life and breath, nor I who set in order the elements within each of you. Therefore the Creator of the world, who shaped the beginning of man and devised the origin of all things, will in his mercy give life and breath back to you again, since you now forget yourselves for the sake of his laws. . . Look at the heaven and the earth and see everything that is in them, and recognize that God did not make them out of things that existed. Thus also mankind comes into being.

levels.title: The Fullness of Time
levels.reflection: In 63 BC the Roman general Pompey took Jerusalem, and the land of the promise came under Roman power. Seen from outside it was a time of occupation; seen from the Gospel, it was the fullness of time. Saint Paul writes that when it had come, God sent his Son, made of a woman, made under the law. Saint Luke places the birth within an empire: a decree went out from Caesar Augustus that the whole world should be enrolled. The Catechism says God has visited his people and fulfilled the promise made to Abraham, acting far beyond all expectation.

scripture.text: But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent his Son, made of a woman, made under the law:

levels.title: Herod the Great
levels.reflection: King Herod ruled Judea under Roman overlordship from 37 BC. He built the great retaining walls of the Temple Mount to enlarge the Second Temple, and he died in Jericho, usually dated to 4 BC. Saint Matthew says Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judah in the days of king Herod, and that wise men came asking where the king of the Jews was born. Herod was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him. The Catechism says the flight into Egypt and the massacre of the innocents make manifest the opposition of darkness to the light. A throne that thinks it is safe is always the first to be afraid.

scripture.text: When Jesus therefore was born in Bethlehem of Juda, in the days of king Herod, behold, there came wise men from the east to Jerusalem. Saying, Where is he that is born king of the Jews? For we have seen his star in the east, and are come to adore him. And king Herod hearing this, was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him.

levels.title: The Ones Who Waited
levels.reflection: While empires came and went, a small remnant waited. The Catechism calls them the people of the poor, who await in hope the "consolation of Israel" and "the redemption of Jerusalem." Saint Luke meets two of them in the Temple. Simeon, just and devout, had been told by the Holy Ghost that he would not see death before he had seen the Christ of the Lord. Anna, a widow of eighty-four years, had not departed from the temple, serving night and day, and she spoke of the child to all who looked for the redemption of Israel. In 1947 a scroll of Isaiah was found at Qumran: the waiting left a written trace.

scripture.text: And behold there was a man in Jerusalem named Simeon, and this man was just and devout, waiting for the consolation of Israel; and the Holy Ghost was in him. And he had received an answer from the Holy Ghost, that he should not see death, before he had seen the Christ of the Lord. And he came by the Spirit into the temple. And when his parents brought in the child Jesus, to do for him according to the custom of the law, He also took him into his arms, and blessed God, and said: Now thou dost dismiss thy servant, O Lord, according to thy word in peace; Because my eyes have seen thy salvation, Which thou hast prepared before the face of all peoples: A light to the revelation of the Gentiles, and the glory of thy people Israel.

levels.title: Daughter of Zion
levels.reflection: Zephaniah tells the daughter of Zion to rejoice: "The king of Israel the Lord is in the midst of thee." When Gabriel greets Mary, the Church hears the same word, "Rejoice," and the same title, Daughter of Zion. She is greeted as "full of grace." The Church teaches that Mary was redeemed from the moment of her conception, which the dogma of the Immaculate Conception confesses: in 1854 Pope Pius IX proclaimed that she was preserved immune from all stain of original sin by the merits of Jesus Christ. Her feast is December 8, in the heart of Advent.

scripture.text: Give praise, O daughter of Sion: shout, O Israel: be glad, and rejoice with all thy heart, O daughter of Jerusalem. The Lord hath taken away thy judgment, he hath turned away thy enemies: the king of Israel the Lord is in the midst of thee, thou shalt fear evil no more. In that day it shall be said to Jerusalem: Fear not: to Sion: Let not thy hands be weakened. The Lord thy God in the midst of thee is mighty, he will save: he will rejoice over thee with gladness, he will be silent in his love, he will be joyful over thee in praise.

saint.name: Pope Pius IX
saint.reference: Ineffabilis Deus (1854), as quoted in CCC 491
saint.text: The most Blessed Virgin Mary was, from the first moment of her conception, by a singular grace and privilege of almighty God and by virtue of the merits of Jesus Christ, Saviour of the human race, preserved immune from all stain of original sin.

levels.title: The Voice in the Wilderness
levels.reflection: "The voice of one crying in the desert: Prepare ye the way of the Lord." Isaiah wrote it, and in the Gospels John the Baptist comes preaching in the desert of Judea and applies it to himself: "I am the voice of one crying out in the wilderness." The Catechism calls him the Lord's immediate precursor, "more than a prophet", the last of the prophets, and the "voice" of the Consoler who is coming. At the end he says the line the Church makes its own in Advent: "He must increase, but I must decrease."

scripture.text: He said: I am the voice of one crying out in the wilderness, make straight the way of the Lord, as said the prophet Isaias.

levels.title: O Wisdom
levels.reflection: On December 17 the Church begins the O Antiphons, sung at Vespers with the Magnificat until December 23. The first is O Sapientia, O Wisdom. The Gospel of the day is the genealogy that opens Matthew: "The book of the generation of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham", closing with "Jacob begot Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ." The Book of Wisdom says wisdom "reacheth from end to end mightily, and ordereth all things sweetly." The promise has been working through every name in that list.

scripture.text: She reacheth therefore from end to end mightily, and ordereth all things sweetly.

levels.title: O Adonai
levels.reflection: December 18: the antiphon is O Adonai ("O Lord"). The Gospel is Joseph's dream. An angel says: "Joseph, son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife ... thou shalt call his name JESUS. For he shall save his people from their sins." At the burning bush God had named himself: "I AM WHO AM." Isaiah says: "The Lord is our judge, the Lord is our lawgiver, the Lord is our king: he will save us." The Catechism says the name Jesus means "God saves". Saint John Paul II's apostolic exhortation Redemptoris Custos is on the person and mission of Saint Joseph.

scripture.text: But while he thought on these things, behold the angel of the Lord appeared to him in his sleep, saying: Joseph, son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife, for that which is conceived in her, is of the Holy Ghost. And she shall bring forth a son: and thou shalt call his name JESUS. For he shall save his people from their sins.

levels.title: O Root of Jesse
levels.reflection: December 19: O Radix Jesse, O Root of Jesse. Isaiah says of that root: "him the Gentiles shall beseech." The Gospel is Zechariah and the angel. "Fear not, Zachary, for thy prayer is heard; and thy wife Elizabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John." The Church sees in the child the Lord's immediate forerunner, filled with the Holy Ghost even from his mother's womb. God's answers arrive late, and larger than the prayer.

scripture.text: But the angel said to him: Fear not, Zachary, for thy prayer is heard; and thy wife Elizabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John: And thou shalt have joy and gladness, and many shall rejoice in his nativity. For he shall be great before the Lord; and shall drink no wine nor strong drink: and he shall be filled with the Holy Ghost, even from his mother's womb. And he shall convert many of the children of Israel to the Lord their God. And he shall go before him in the spirit and power of Elias; that he may turn the hearts of the fathers unto the children, and the incredulous to the wisdom of the just, to prepare unto the Lord a perfect people.

levels.title: O Key of David
levels.reflection: December 20: O Clavis David, O Key of David. Isaiah says: "I will lay the key of the house of David upon his shoulder: and he shall open, and none shall shut." The Book of Revelation gives the title to Christ: "he that hath the key of David; he that openeth, and no man shutteth." The Gospel is the Annunciation. Gabriel tells Mary she will conceive, and that the Lord God shall give her son the throne of David his father. She answers: "Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it done to me according to thy word." The Catechism says her virginity is the sign of her faith.

scripture.text: And the angel said to her: Fear not, Mary, for thou hast found grace with God. Behold thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and shalt bring forth a son; and thou shalt call his name Jesus. He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the most High; and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of David his father; and he shall reign in the house of Jacob for ever. And of his kingdom there shall be no end.

levels.title: O Dawn of the East
levels.reflection: December 21: O Oriens, O Dawn of the East. Malachi promises: "the Sun of justice shall arise, and health in his wings." The Gospel is the Visitation. When Elizabeth hears Mary's greeting the infant leaps in her womb, and she cries out: "whence is this to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?" David had once asked, "How shall the ark of the Lord come to me?" The Catechism calls Mary the ark of the covenant, the place where the glory of the Lord dwells. Light arrives in the dark by being carried.

scripture.text: And it came to pass, that when Elizabeth heard the salutation of Mary, the infant leaped in her womb. And Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Ghost: And she cried out with a loud voice, and said: Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb. And whence is this to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me? For behold as soon as the voice of thy salutation sounded in my ears, the infant in my womb leaped for joy. And blessed art thou that hast believed, because those things shall be accomplished that were spoken to thee by the Lord.

levels.title: O King of the Nations
levels.reflection: December 22: O Rex Gentium, O King of the Nations. The Gospel is the Magnificat. "My soul doth magnify the Lord ... he hath regarded the humility of his handmaid; for behold from henceforth all generations shall call me blessed." Centuries earlier a song rose in the books of Kings: "My heart hath rejoiced in the Lord ... He raiseth up the needy from the dust." The Catechism calls the Magnificat the song both of the Mother of God and of the Church, and of the "poor" whose hope is met by the fulfillment of the promises made to our ancestors. Mary ends by naming Abraham.

scripture.text: And Mary said: My soul doth magnify the Lord. And my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour. Because he hath regarded the humility of his handmaid; for behold from henceforth all generations shall call me blessed. Because he that is mighty, hath done great things to me; and holy is his name. And his mercy is from generation unto generations, to them that fear him. He hath shewed might in his arm: he hath scattered the proud in the conceit of their heart. He hath put down the mighty from their seat, and hath exalted the humble. He hath filled the hungry with good things; and the rich he hath sent empty away. He hath received Israel his servant, being mindful of his mercy: As he spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and to his seed for ever.

levels.title: O Emmanuel
levels.reflection: December 23: O Emmanuel, the last of the seven O Antiphons, which the Church sings at Vespers from December 17 to 23. If you read the first letters of the titles from last to first, they appear to form the Latin ERO CRAS: "Tomorrow I will be there." The Gospel is the birth and naming of John: "Not so; but he shall be called John." Isaiah had promised a virgin who would bear a son called Emmanuel, and the Catechism says that in the fullness of time the Holy Spirit completes in Mary all the preparations, and the Father gives the world Emmanuel, "God-with-us".

scripture.text: Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign. Behold a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and his name shall be called Emmanuel.

saint.name: St. Athanasius
saint.reference: De incarnatione 54, 3, as quoted in CCC 460
saint.text: For the Son of God became man so that we might become God.

levels.title: Christmas Eve: The Promise Has a Name
levels.reflection: The promise that began in the garden now stands at the door of Bethlehem. Micah had named the town: "And thou, Bethlehem Ephrata, art a little one among the thousands of Juda: out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be the ruler in Israel." Saint Luke tells how it came to be: a decree from Caesar Augustus, and Joseph going up from Nazareth to the city of David. This morning's Gospel is the canticle of Zechariah: "Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; because he hath visited and wrought the redemption of his people." Tonight the promise has a name.

scripture.text: AND THOU, BETHLEHEM Ephrata, art a little one among the thousands of Juda: out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be the ruler in Israel: and his going forth is from the beginning, from the days of eternity.

saint.name: St. Leo the Great
saint.reference: Sermo 22 in nativitate Domini, as quoted in CCC 1691
saint.text: Christian, recognize your dignity and, now that you share in God's own nature, do not return to your former base condition by sinning. Remember who is your head and of whose body you are a member. Never forget that you have been rescued from the power of darkness and brought into the light of the Kingdom of God.

questions.prompt: What does the Church do each year when she celebrates the liturgy of Advent?
choices: She repeats the forty days of Christ's fast in the desert
She makes present the ancient expectancy of the Messiah
She celebrates the baptism of the Lord
questions.correctAnswer: She makes present the ancient expectancy of the Messiah
questions.explanation: The Catechism says that in the liturgy of Advent the Church makes present this ancient expectancy of the Messiah, sharing in the long preparation for the Savior's first coming.

questions.prompt: True or False: Advent looks back to Christ's first coming and also renews the desire for his second coming.
questions.explanation: By sharing in the long preparation for the first coming, the faithful renew their ardent desire for his second coming.

questions.prompt: In Matthew 24:42, what reason does the Lord give for watching?
choices: Because the prophets have fallen silent
Because the Temple will soon be destroyed
Because you know not what hour your Lord will come
questions.correctAnswer: Because you know not what hour your Lord will come
questions.explanation: The Douay-Rheims reads: "Watch ye therefore, because ye know not what hour your Lord will come."

questions.prompt: Maranatha, the early Christian prayer, means "Our Lord, ____!"
questions.explanation: Maranatha is Aramaic for "Our Lord, come!" Christians pray it above all in the Eucharist to hasten Christ's return.

questions.prompt: What does the Church call Genesis 3:15, the first announcement of the Messiah and Redeemer?
choices: The Shema, or "hear, O Israel" of the Law
The Decalogue, or "ten words" of the Law
The Magnificat, or "song of the handmaid"
questions.explanation: The Catechism calls this passage the Protoevangelium ("first gospel"): the first announcement of the Messiah and Redeemer.

questions.prompt: True or False: Christian tradition sees in Genesis 3:15 an announcement of the "New Adam", who makes amends for the disobedience of Adam.
questions.explanation: The Christian tradition sees in this passage the New Adam, who became obedient unto death, even death on a cross.

questions.prompt: According to Romans 5:19, what did one man's obedience do for many?
choices: Many were left without a law
questions.explanation: The Douay-Rheims reads: "as by the disobedience of one man, many were made sinners; so also by the obedience of one, many shall be made just."

questions.prompt: Whom have many Fathers and Doctors of the Church seen in the woman announced in the Protoevangelium?
choices: Judith, the heroine who saved her people
Mary Magdalene, the first witness of the Resurrection
Mary, the mother of Christ, the "new Eve"
Sarah, the wife of Abraham and mother of the promised son
questions.correctAnswer: Mary, the mother of Christ, the "new Eve"
questions.explanation: Many Fathers and Doctors of the Church have seen in the woman Mary, the mother of Christ, the "new Eve".

questions.prompt: What does God make of Abram when he calls him from his country, his kindred and his father's house?
choices: Isaac, "the heir of the covenant and its first priest"
Abraham, "the father of a multitude of nations"
Moses, "the lawgiver of a chosen people"
David, "the shepherd of a great kingdom"
questions.correctAnswer: Abraham, "the father of a multitude of nations"
questions.explanation: God calls Abram and makes him Abraham, that is, "the father of a multitude of nations".

questions.prompt: True or False: According to Galatians 3:16, the promises were made to Abraham and to his seeds, as of many.
questions.explanation: No: "He saith not, And to his seeds, as of many: but as of one, And to thy seed, which is Christ."

questions.prompt: When Isaac asked where the lamb was, what did Abraham answer in the Douay-Rheims (Genesis 22:8)?
choices: We shall find a ram caught fast in the thicket nearby
The Lord has no need of a victim from his servants
God will provide himself a victim for an holocaust
The shepherds will bring a lamb from the flock at dawn
questions.correctAnswer: God will provide himself a victim for an holocaust
questions.explanation: Genesis 22:8 in the Douay-Rheims: "God will provide himself a victim for an holocaust, my son."

questions.prompt: True or False: The people descended from Abraham were called to prepare for the day when God would gather all his children into the unity of the Church.
questions.explanation: The Catechism says they would be the trustee of the promise, called to prepare for that day, and the root onto which the Gentiles would be grafted.

questions.prompt: In Exodus 12:13, what sign was to protect the houses of the Israelites?
questions.explanation: "And the blood shall be unto you for a sign in the houses where you shall be: and I shall see the blood, and shall pass over you."

questions.prompt: What did John the Baptist say when he saw Jesus coming to him?
choices: Behold the Son of David, who shall sit upon his father's throne
Behold the Lamb of God, who taketh away the sin of the world
Behold the new Moses, who shall lead the people to freedom
Behold the King of Israel, who cometh in the name of the Lord
questions.correctAnswer: Behold the Lamb of God, who taketh away the sin of the world
questions.explanation: John 1:29 in the Douay-Rheims. John thus reveals Jesus as the suffering Servant and as the Paschal Lamb.

questions.prompt: True or False: In Acts 3:22 Saint Peter says that the Lord will raise up a prophet from among the Gentiles.
questions.explanation: No: "A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you of your brethren, like unto me."

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, what did Jesus do at the Last Supper in the course of the Passover meal?
choices: He moved the Passover to a different season of the year
He abolished the Passover and gave it no meaning at all
He gave the Jewish Passover its definitive meaning
He celebrated the Passover for the first time with his apostles
questions.correctAnswer: He gave the Jewish Passover its definitive meaning
questions.explanation: By celebrating the Last Supper in the course of the Passover meal, Jesus gave the Jewish Passover its definitive meaning.

questions.prompt: In Numbers 24:17, what shall rise out of Jacob?
questions.explanation: "A star shall rise out of Jacob and a sceptre shall spring up from Israel."

questions.prompt: In Genesis 49:10, who shall be "the expectation of nations"?
choices: The priest who serves in the Temple, after the exile
The judge of Israel, who rules the tribes in the desert
He that is to be sent, when the scepter departs from Judah
Moses the lawgiver, who led the tribes out of Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: He that is to be sent, when the scepter departs from Judah
questions.explanation: "The sceptre shall not be taken away from Juda ... till he come that is to be sent, and he shall be the expectation of nations."

questions.prompt: True or False: The Catechism sees in the Magi the first-fruits of the nations who welcome the good news of salvation.
questions.explanation: "In the magi, representatives of the neighbouring pagan religions, the Gospel sees the first-fruits of the nations."

questions.prompt: In Apocalypse 5:5, how is the one who has prevailed to open the book described?
choices: The morning star of Jacob, the scepter of Israel
The lion of the tribe of Judah, the root of David
The Lamb of Zion, the servant of the Lord
The rock of Zion, the shepherd of the flock of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: The lion of the tribe of Judah, the root of David
questions.explanation: "Behold the lion of the tribe of Juda, the root of David, hath prevailed to open the book."

questions.prompt: In the promise of 2 Kings 7:13 about David's seed, what does God say about the throne of his kingdom?
choices: It will end with the Exile and the fall of the city
It will be given to the priests of the Temple
It will pass to the house of Saul after Solomon
He will establish the throne of his kingdom for ever
questions.correctAnswer: He will establish the throne of his kingdom for ever
questions.explanation: "I will raise up thy seed after thee ... and I will establish the throne of his kingdom for ever."

questions.prompt: True or False: In Luke 1:32-33 the angel tells Mary that of her son's kingdom there shall be an end.
questions.explanation: No: "And of his kingdom there shall be no end."

questions.prompt: Which Gospel begins with "The book of the generation of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham"?
questions.explanation: Matthew 1:1 begins the genealogy of Jesus with the two promises, David and Abraham.

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, what did Jesus accept in the title "Son of David"?
choices: He refused the title because it belonged to the high priest
He used the title only in private conversation with Peter
He accepted his rightful title of Messiah, though with some reserve
He gave the title away to John the Baptist at the Jordan
questions.correctAnswer: He accepted his rightful title of Messiah, though with some reserve
questions.explanation: Jesus accepted his rightful title of Messiah, though with some reserve because it was understood by some of his contemporaries in too human a sense, as essentially political.

questions.prompt: In 3 Kings 8:10-11, what filled the house of the Lord when the priests came out of the sanctuary?
choices: A great light from the east
questions.explanation: "A cloud filled the house of the Lord ... for the glory of the Lord had filled the house of the Lord."

questions.prompt: What does Solomon say cannot contain God?
choices: The cloud that filled the house of the Lord
The ark of the covenant and the holy of holies
The Temple courts and all the land of Israel
Heaven, and the heavens of heavens
questions.correctAnswer: Heaven, and the heavens of heavens
questions.explanation: "If heaven, and the heavens of heavens cannot contain thee, how much less this house which I have built?"

questions.prompt: According to John 1:14, what did the Word do?
choices: The Word spoke from the mountain to the fathers
The Word came down from heaven in a cloud of glory
The Word was made flesh and dwelt among us
The Word was written on tablets of stone for Moses
questions.correctAnswer: The Word was made flesh and dwelt among us
questions.explanation: John 1:14 in the Douay-Rheims: "And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us."

questions.prompt: True or False: According to John 2:21, when Jesus spoke of raising up the temple in three days, he meant the Temple at Jerusalem.
questions.explanation: No: "But he spoke of the temple of his body."

questions.prompt: What did the people say when the fire of the Lord fell on Mount Carmel?
choices: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord
Hosanna to the Son of David
Let us go up to the house of the Lord
The Lord he is God, the Lord he is God
questions.correctAnswer: The Lord he is God, the Lord he is God
questions.explanation: 3 Kings 18:39 in the Douay-Rheims: "they fell on their faces, and they said: The Lord he is God, the Lord he is God."

questions.prompt: In Malachias 4:5, whom does the Lord promise to send before the great and dreadful day?
questions.explanation: "Behold I will send you Elias the prophet, before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord."

questions.prompt: True or False: According to the Catechism, Elijah is called the "father" of the prophets.
questions.explanation: "Elijah is the 'father' of the prophets, 'the generation of those who seek him, who seek the face of the God of Jacob.'"

questions.prompt: In Luke 1:17, in whose spirit and power does the angel say John will go before the Lord?
questions.explanation: "And he shall go before him in the spirit and power of Elias." The Catechism calls John "Elijah (who) must come".

questions.prompt: In Isaias 7:14, what name is the child to be called?
questions.explanation: "Behold a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and his name shall be called Emmanuel."

questions.prompt: According to Matthew 1:23, what does "Emmanuel" mean when interpreted?
questions.explanation: "Behold a virgin shall be with child, and bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us."

questions.prompt: True or False: The Church teaches that Jesus was conceived by the Holy Spirit together with the seed of Joseph.
questions.explanation: No: Jesus was conceived "by the Holy Spirit without human seed".

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, in what does the Church see the fulfillment of the promise given through Isaiah?
choices: The birth of John the Baptist
questions.explanation: The Gospel accounts understand the virginal conception as a divine work, and the Church sees here the fulfillment of the promise: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive and bear a son."

questions.prompt: In Isaias 9:2, who have seen a great light?
choices: The shepherds who watched their flocks by night
The priests who served in the house of the Lord
The people that walked in darkness
The kings of the earth who sat upon their thrones
questions.correctAnswer: The people that walked in darkness
questions.explanation: "The people that walked in darkness, have seen a great light: to them that dwelt in the region of the shadow of death, light is risen."

questions.prompt: Which of these is one of the names given to the child in Isaias 9:6?
questions.explanation: "His name shall be called, Wonderful, Counsellor, God the Mighty, the Father of the world to come, the Prince of Peace."

questions.prompt: In Isaias 11:1, out of whose root does the rod come forth?
questions.explanation: "And there shall come forth a rod out of the root of Jesse." The Catechism points to the first two verses of Isaiah 11 for the characteristics of the awaited Messiah.

questions.prompt: True or False: According to the Catechism, the seven gifts of the Holy Spirit belong in their fullness to the prophets alone.
questions.explanation: No: "They belong in their fullness to Christ, Son of David."

questions.prompt: In Isaias 53:5, what is the effect of the servant's bruises?
choices: By his bruises we are warned
By his bruises the Temple is rebuilt
By his bruises we are healed
By his bruises the nations are scattered
questions.correctAnswer: By his bruises we are healed
questions.explanation: "He was wounded for our iniquities, he was bruised for our sins: ... and by his bruises we are healed."

questions.prompt: In Acts 8, what did Philip do when the Ethiopian asked of whom the prophet was speaking?
choices: He sent him to Jerusalem to ask the high priest
He told him to read on until the feast of Easter
He baptized him at once, without speaking of the prophet
Beginning at this scripture, he preached unto him Jesus
questions.correctAnswer: Beginning at this scripture, he preached unto him Jesus
questions.explanation: "Then Philip, opening his mouth, and beginning at this scripture, preached unto him Jesus."

questions.prompt: True or False: The Catechism teaches that Jesus' redemptive death has no connection with Isaiah's prophecy of the suffering Servant.
questions.explanation: No: "In particular Jesus' redemptive death fulfils Isaiah's prophecy of the suffering Servant."

questions.prompt: According to 1 Peter 2:24, where did Christ bear our sins in his body?
questions.explanation: "Who his own self bore our sins in his body upon the tree: that we, being dead to sins, should live to justice: by whose stripes you were healed."

questions.prompt: What command opens Isaias 40?
choices: Be comforted, be comforted, my people
Arise, shine, for thy light is come
Repent, for the kingdom is at hand
questions.correctAnswer: Be comforted, be comforted, my people
questions.explanation: "Be comforted, be comforted, my people, saith your God."

questions.prompt: In Jeremias 31:33, where does God say he will write his law in the new covenant?
choices: In a book kept in the Temple
On the doorposts of the house
questions.explanation: "I will give my law in their bowels, and I will write it in their heart: and I will be their God, and they shall be my people."

questions.prompt: True or False: In Ezechiel 36:26 God promises to take away the stony heart and give a heart of flesh.
questions.explanation: "And I will give you a new heart, and put a new spirit within you: and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and will give you a heart of flesh."

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, what is the Exile in God's plan?
choices: A proof that the covenant had ended and the promises of God had failed entirely
The final fulfillment of all the promises made to Abraham and to David
A punishment with no purpose and no promise of a return for the people
The mysterious fidelity of the Savior God and the beginning of a promised restoration
questions.correctAnswer: The mysterious fidelity of the Savior God and the beginning of a promised restoration
questions.explanation: The Exile is "apparently the failure of the promises, which is in fact the mysterious fidelity of the Savior God and the beginning of a promised restoration, but according to the Spirit."

questions.prompt: In Daniel 7:13, with what does the one like the son of man come?
questions.explanation: "Lo, one like the son of man came with the clouds of heaven, and he came even to the Ancient of days."

questions.prompt: True or False: According to Daniel 7:14, the kingdom given to the son of man shall be destroyed after a thousand years.
questions.explanation: No: his power "is an everlasting power that shall not be taken away: and his kingdom that shall not be destroyed."

questions.prompt: In Mark 14:62, how does Jesus answer the high priest's question whether he is the Christ?
choices: Ask those who heard me teach in the Temple, for they know what I have said
I am, and you shall see the Son of man sitting on the right hand of the power of God
Thou hast said it, but tell no man what thou hast heard or seen of me
My hour is not yet come, neither shall ye see the Son of man in glory
questions.correctAnswer: I am, and you shall see the Son of man sitting on the right hand of the power of God
questions.explanation: "And Jesus said to him: I am. And you shall see the Son of man sitting on the right hand of the power of God, and coming with the clouds of heaven."

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, what does Christ's being seated at the Father's right hand signify?
choices: The end of his mission on earth, once the Temple had been rebuilt in Jerusalem
The inauguration of the Messiah's kingdom, fulfilling Daniel's vision of the Son of man
A time of rest for the Messiah before the Passion and the day of his arrest
The restoration of the earthly kingdom of David with its throne in Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: The inauguration of the Messiah's kingdom, fulfilling Daniel's vision of the Son of man
questions.explanation: "Being seated at the Father's right hand signifies the inauguration of the Messiah's kingdom, the fulfilment of the prophet Daniel's vision concerning the Son of man."

questions.prompt: In Malachias 3:1, whom does the Lord send to prepare the way before his face?
questions.explanation: "Behold I send my angel, and he shall prepare the way before my face."

questions.prompt: According to Hebrews 1:1-2, how has God spoken to us in these last days?
questions.explanation: "God, who, at sundry times and in divers manners, spoke in times past to the fathers by the prophets, last of all, in these days hath spoken to us by his Son."

questions.prompt: True or False: According to the Catechism, further Revelation is still to come after Christ.
questions.explanation: No: "the Son is his Father's definitive Word; so there will be no further Revelation after him."

questions.prompt: Which Gospel begins with the words of Isaiah and Malachi about a messenger sent before the Lord's face?
questions.explanation: Mark 1:2 opens the Gospel: "As it is written in Isaias the prophet: Behold I send my angel before thy face, who shall prepare the way before thee."

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, what does the mother of seven sons teach them about creation?
choices: That the world has always existed and will never pass away
That creation was the work of angels who served the Creator
That God did not make heaven and earth out of things that existed
That the heavens are older than the earth and all that is in it
questions.correctAnswer: That God did not make heaven and earth out of things that existed
questions.explanation: "Look at the heaven and the earth and see everything that is in them, and recognize that God did not make them out of things that existed."

questions.prompt: True or False: The Catechism says the Maccabean martyrs confessed their hope of being raised again by God.
questions.explanation: "One cannot but choose to die at the hands of men and to cherish the hope that God gives of being raised again by him."

questions.prompt: In John 10:22, which feast was being kept at Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: "And it was the feast of the dedication at Jerusalem: and it was winter."

questions.prompt: True or False: The Catechism teaches that prayer for the dead can neither help them nor make their intercession for us effective.
questions.explanation: No: "Our prayer for them is capable not only of helping them, but also of making their intercession for us effective."

questions.prompt: According to Galatians 4:4, what happened when the fulness of the time was come?
choices: God gave a new law upon a mountain in the desert
God raised up a king from Judah to rule the nations
God sent his Son, made of a woman, made under the law
God sent a great prophet to preach to all the nations
questions.correctAnswer: God sent his Son, made of a woman, made under the law
questions.explanation: "But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent his Son, made of a woman, made under the law."

questions.prompt: True or False: According to the Catechism, the sending of the Son fulfills the promise God made to Abraham and his descendants.
questions.explanation: "God has visited his people. He has fulfilled the promise he made to Abraham and his descendants."

questions.prompt: In Luke 2:1, who issued the decree that the whole world should be enrolled?
questions.explanation: "There went out a decree from Caesar Augustus, that the whole world should be enrolled." Quirinius is named as governor of Syria, but the decree is Caesar's.

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, what does the Annunciation to Mary inaugurate?
choices: The reign of Herod, the king of Judea under the power of Rome
The end of the prophets and the long silence of heaven over Israel
The rebuilding of the Temple on the mountain of Zion by the returned exiles
"The fullness of time", the fulfillment of God's promises and preparations
questions.correctAnswer: "The fullness of time", the fulfillment of God's promises and preparations
questions.explanation: "The Annunciation to Mary inaugurates 'the fullness of time', the time of the fulfilment of God's promises and preparations."

questions.prompt: In Matthew 2:1-3, how did king Herod react when he heard the wise men ask where the king of the Jews was born?
choices: He was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him
He ordered the wise men to be arrested at the gate
He ignored them, for he had no fear of a king to come
He rejoiced at once and sent gifts with the wise men
questions.correctAnswer: He was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him
questions.explanation: "And king Herod hearing this, was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him."

questions.prompt: According to Matthew 2:1, in what town was Jesus born?
questions.explanation: "When Jesus therefore was born in Bethlehem of Juda, in the days of king Herod, behold, there came wise men from the east to Jerusalem."

questions.prompt: True or False: According to the Catechism, the flight into Egypt and the massacre of the innocents make manifest the opposition of darkness to the light.
questions.explanation: "The flight into Egypt and the massacre of the innocents make manifest the opposition of darkness to the light."

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, what does Jesus' departure from Egypt recall?
choices: The journey of Abraham, presenting him as the father of many nations
The Exile in Babylon, presenting him as the returning remnant
The Exodus, presenting him as the definitive liberator of God's people
The crossing of the Jordan, presenting him as a new Joshua
questions.correctAnswer: The Exodus, presenting him as the definitive liberator of God's people
questions.explanation: "Jesus' departure from Egypt recalls the exodus and presents him as the definitive liberator of God's people."

questions.prompt: In Luke 2:25, for what was Simeon waiting?
questions.explanation: "This man was just and devout, waiting for the consolation of Israel; and the Holy Ghost was in him."

questions.prompt: What did the Holy Ghost promise Simeon?
choices: That he should not see death before he had seen the Christ of the Lord
That he would live to see the Gentiles come to the Temple
That he would be named high priest of the Temple
That he would see Jerusalem restored before he died
questions.correctAnswer: That he should not see death before he had seen the Christ of the Lord
questions.explanation: "He had received an answer from the Holy Ghost, that he should not see death, before he had seen the Christ of the Lord."

questions.prompt: True or False: According to Luke 2:36-38, Anna was a young woman who told no one about the child.
questions.explanation: No: she was a widow "until fourscore and four years", and she "spoke of him to all that looked for the redemption of Israel."

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, what does the presentation of Jesus in the temple show him to be?
choices: The new high priest of the Temple
The firstborn Son who belongs to the Lord
questions.correctAnswer: The firstborn Son who belongs to the Lord
questions.explanation: "The presentation of Jesus in the temple shows him to be the firstborn Son who belongs to the Lord. With Simeon and Anna, all Israel awaits its encounter with the Saviour."

questions.prompt: In Luke 1:28, how does the angel greet Mary?
choices: Hail, full of grace, the Lord is with thee
Blessed art thou, daughter of David
questions.correctAnswer: Hail, full of grace, the Lord is with thee
questions.explanation: "And the angel being come in, said unto her: Hail, full of grace, the Lord is with thee: blessed art thou among women."

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, with what title was it "quite correct" for the angel Gabriel to greet Mary?
questions.explanation: "It was quite correct for the angel Gabriel to greet her as the 'Daughter of Zion': 'Rejoice.'"

questions.prompt: True or False: In 1854 Pope Pius IX proclaimed the dogma of the Immaculate Conception.
questions.explanation: The dogma of the Immaculate Conception confesses that Mary was redeemed from the moment of her conception, "as Pope Pius IX proclaimed in 1854".

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, from where does Mary's "splendour of an entirely unique holiness" come?
choices: From the prayers of the prophets
questions.explanation: "The 'splendour of an entirely unique holiness' by which Mary is 'enriched from the first instant of her conception' comes wholly from Christ."

questions.prompt: According to Matthew 3:1-3, what did John the Baptist preach in the desert of Judea?
choices: Return to the land of your fathers, for it is time
Fast and keep vigil, for the Lamb of God is come
Do penance: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand
Rebuild the Temple, for the day of the Lord is near
questions.correctAnswer: Do penance: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand
questions.explanation: "In those days cometh John the Baptist preaching in the desert of Judea. And saying: Do penance: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand."

questions.prompt: In John 1:23, how does John describe himself?
choices: The Messiah, whom the prophets had foretold
The voice of one crying out in the wilderness
Elijah come again, as the prophet Malachi promised
The prophet like Moses, whom the people must hear
questions.correctAnswer: The voice of one crying out in the wilderness
questions.explanation: "I am the voice of one crying out in the wilderness, make straight the way of the Lord, as said the prophet Isaias."

questions.prompt: True or False: According to the Catechism, John the Baptist is the first of the prophets.
questions.explanation: No: "John surpasses all the prophets, of whom he is the last."

questions.prompt: John says of Jesus in John 3:30: "He must ____, but I must decrease."
questions.explanation: "He must increase, but I must decrease." The Church unites herself to John's desire by celebrating his birth and martyrdom.

questions.prompt: According to the Book of Wisdom 8:1, how does wisdom reach "from end to end"?
questions.explanation: "She reacheth therefore from end to end mightily, and ordereth all things sweetly."

questions.prompt: According to Matthew 1:16, of whom was Jesus born?
choices: Anna, the prophetess of the Temple
Rachel, the mother of the patriarch Joseph
questions.explanation: "And Jacob begot Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

questions.prompt: True or False: According to the Catechism, Joseph was called by God to take Mary as his wife so that Jesus would be born into the messianic lineage of David.
questions.explanation: "God called Joseph to 'take Mary as your wife' ... so that Jesus, 'who is called Christ', should be born of Joseph's spouse into the messianic lineage of David."

questions.prompt: In Romans 1:3, from whom was God's Son made according to the flesh?
questions.explanation: "Concerning his Son, who was made to him of the seed of David, according to the flesh."

questions.prompt: What name does the angel tell Joseph to give the child in Matthew 1:21?
questions.explanation: "And she shall bring forth a son: and thou shalt call his name JESUS. For he shall save his people from their sins."

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, what does the name "Jesus" mean in Hebrew?
questions.explanation: "Jesus means in Hebrew: 'God saves.'"

questions.prompt: In Exodus 3:14, how does God name himself to Moses?
choices: The God of thy fathers alone
questions.explanation: "God said to Moses: I AM WHO AM. He said: Thus shalt thou say to the children of Israel: HE WHO IS, hath sent me to you."

questions.prompt: Which apostolic exhortation of Pope Saint John Paul II (1989) is on the person and mission of Saint Joseph?
questions.explanation: Redemptoris Custos, of August 15, 1989, is on the person and mission of Saint Joseph in the life of Christ and of the Church.

questions.prompt: In Isaias 11:10, whom shall the Gentiles beseech?
questions.explanation: "In that day the root of Jesse, who standeth for an ensign of the people, him the Gentiles shall beseech."

questions.prompt: What name did the angel tell Zechariah to give his son in Luke 1:13?
questions.explanation: "Thy wife Elizabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John."

questions.prompt: True or False: According to Luke 1:15, John would be filled with the Holy Ghost only after he was baptized.
questions.explanation: No: "he shall be filled with the Holy Ghost, even from his mother's womb."

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, what is John the Baptist to the Lord?
choices: His immediate precursor or forerunner, sent to prepare his way
His successor as the prophet of the Most High over the people of Israel
His teacher in the desert, who trained him before the baptism in the Jordan
The first of the twelve apostles, sent out to preach to the house of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: His immediate precursor or forerunner, sent to prepare his way
questions.explanation: "St. John the Baptist is the Lord's immediate precursor or forerunner, sent to prepare his way."

questions.prompt: In Isaias 22:22, what does the Lord lay upon the shoulder of his servant?
choices: The key of the house of David
questions.correctAnswer: The key of the house of David
questions.explanation: "And I will lay the key of the house of David upon his shoulder: and he shall open, and none shall shut."

questions.prompt: How does Mary answer the angel in Luke 1:38?
choices: How shall this be done, because I know not man?
Let it be to me as the prophets have said of old
Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it done to me according to thy word
My soul doth magnify the Lord, and my spirit hath rejoiced
questions.correctAnswer: Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it done to me according to thy word
questions.explanation: "And Mary said: Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it done to me according to thy word." The Catechism calls this "the obedience of faith".

questions.prompt: True or False: According to the Catechism, Mary's virginity is the sign of her faith "unadulterated by any doubt".
questions.explanation: "Mary is a virgin because her virginity is the sign of her faith 'unadulterated by any doubt', and of her undivided gift of herself to God's will."

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, what does the Annunciation inaugurate?
questions.explanation: "The Annunciation to Mary inaugurates 'the fullness of time', the time of the fulfilment of God's promises and preparations."

questions.prompt: In Malachias 4:2, who shall arise "with health in his wings"?
questions.explanation: "Unto you that fear my name, the Sun of justice shall arise, and health in his wings."

questions.prompt: What happened in Elizabeth's womb when she heard Mary's greeting (Luke 1:41)?
choices: The infant was blessed by Gabriel
questions.explanation: "When Elizabeth heard the salutation of Mary, the infant leaped in her womb. And Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Ghost."

questions.prompt: True or False: In 2 Kings 6:9, David asked, "How shall the ark of the Lord come to me?"
questions.explanation: "And David was afraid of the Lord that day, saying: How shall the ark of the Lord come to me?"

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, what is Mary in whom the Lord has made his dwelling?
choices: The tabernacle of Moses, the tent of meeting
The new temple of Solomon, the house of the Lord
The daughter of Zion in person, the ark of the covenant
The mother of the apostles, the queen of the angels
questions.correctAnswer: The daughter of Zion in person, the ark of the covenant
questions.explanation: "Mary, in whom the Lord himself has just made his dwelling, is the daughter of Zion in person, the ark of the covenant, the place where the glory of the Lord dwells."

questions.prompt: What does Mary say in Luke 1:46 that her soul does?
questions.explanation: "And Mary said: My soul doth magnify the Lord. And my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour."

questions.prompt: According to the Magnificat, what has the Lord done to the mighty and to the humble?
choices: He hath given the mighty the earth, and the humble the sea
He hath hidden the humble from the proud in the day of trouble
He hath made the mighty his servants, and the humble his friends
He hath put down the mighty from their seat, and hath exalted the humble
questions.correctAnswer: He hath put down the mighty from their seat, and hath exalted the humble
questions.explanation: "He hath put down the mighty from their seat, and hath exalted the humble."

questions.prompt: True or False: According to the Catechism, the Magnificat is the song of the "poor" whose hope is met by the fulfillment of the promises made to our ancestors.
questions.explanation: The Magnificat is "the song of the 'poor' whose hope is met by the fulfillment of the promises made to our ancestors, 'to Abraham and to his posterity for ever.'"

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, how did Mary adore God in the Magnificat?
choices: She asked for a sign, that she might know the word of the angel was true
She humbled herself, confessing with gratitude that he has done great things and holy is his name
She offered a sacrifice of lambs in the Temple at Jerusalem, as the Law required
She recalled the Exodus alone, giving thanks for the crossing of the sea
questions.correctAnswer: She humbled herself, confessing with gratitude that he has done great things and holy is his name
questions.explanation: "To adore God is to praise and exalt him and to humble oneself, as Mary did in the Magnificat."

questions.prompt: True or False: In Luke 1:61, Elizabeth's neighbors said that none of her kindred was called by the name John.
questions.explanation: "And they said to her: There is none of thy kindred that is called by this name."

questions.prompt: What did Zechariah write on the writing table in Luke 1:63?
questions.explanation: "And demanding a writing table, he wrote, saying: John is his name. And they all wondered."

questions.prompt: What did Elizabeth say the child must be called, in Luke 1:60?
questions.explanation: "And his mother answering, said: Not so; but he shall be called John."

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, what does the Father give the world by the action of the Holy Spirit in Mary?
choices: A new law, written on tablets of stone
A new temple, built by the hands of the faithful
A new prophet, to speak in the name of the Lord
questions.explanation: "By the action of the Holy Spirit in her, the Father gives the world Emmanuel 'God-with-us' (Mt 1:23)."

questions.prompt: In Micheas 5:2, which town is named as the place from which the ruler in Israel shall come forth?
questions.explanation: "And thou, Bethlehem Ephrata, art a little one among the thousands of Juda: out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be the ruler in Israel."

questions.prompt: According to Luke 2:4-5, why did Joseph go up to Bethlehem?
choices: Because Herod summoned him to the palace at Jerusalem to answer for the child
Because he was of the house and family of David, to be enrolled with Mary
To present the child in the Temple on the fortieth day after his birth
To escape the census that had been ordered in the town of Nazareth
questions.correctAnswer: Because he was of the house and family of David, to be enrolled with Mary
questions.explanation: "Joseph also went up from Galilee ... to the city of David, which is called Bethlehem: because he was of the house and family of David, to be enrolled with Mary his espoused wife."

questions.prompt: True or False: According to the Catechism, kings were the first witnesses to the birth of Jesus.
questions.explanation: No: "Simple shepherds were the first witnesses to this event."

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, what is Christmas the mystery of?
choices: The founding of the Church, in which Peter was made its rock by the Lord
The first miracle, in which water was changed into wine at the wedding feast
The giving of the Law, in which God spoke to Moses from the mountain in fire
The "marvellous exchange", in which man's Creator became man and we are made sharers in his divinity
questions.correctAnswer: The "marvellous exchange", in which man's Creator became man and we are made sharers in his divinity
questions.explanation: "Christmas is the mystery of this 'marvellous exchange'": "O marvellous exchange! Man's Creator has become man, born of the Virgin. We have been made sharers in the divinity of Christ who humbled himself to share our humanity."

questions.prompt: True or False: Advent looks only back to Christ's first coming at Bethlehem.
questions.explanation: Advent makes present the ancient expectancy of the Messiah, and the faithful also "renew their ardent desire for his second coming".

questions.prompt: Which liturgical color is used in Advent?
questions.explanation: "Violet or purple is used in Advent and Lent."

citations.reference: General Instruction of the Roman Missal 346

questions.prompt: True or False: On the Sundays of Advent the Gloria is sung at Mass.
questions.explanation: The Gloria "is sung or said on Sundays outside the Seasons of Advent and Lent, on solemnities and feasts, and at special celebrations of a more solemn character."

citations.reference: General Instruction of the Roman Missal 53

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, in which seasons does the Church especially re-read and re-live the great events of salvation history in the "today" of her liturgy?
choices: Advent and Lent, and above all at the Easter Vigil
Advent and Pentecost, and above all at the Epiphany
Ordinary Time, and above all on Sundays in summer
Christmas and Easter, and above all at Pentecost
questions.correctAnswer: Advent and Lent, and above all at the Easter Vigil
questions.explanation: "The Church, especially during Advent and Lent and above all at the Easter Vigil, re-reads and re-lives the great events of salvation history in the 'today' of her liturgy."

questions.prompt: In Luke 21:36, with what does the Lord join watching?
questions.explanation: "Watch ye, therefore, praying at all times, that you may be accounted worthy to escape all these things that are to come, and to stand before the Son of man."

questions.prompt: In Titus 2:13, for what does Saint Paul say Christians are looking?
choices: The rebuilding of Jerusalem and the return of the exiles from Babylon
The restoration of the kingdom to Israel under a son of David
The return of the prophets and the end of the age of the Law
The blessed hope and coming of the glory of the great God and our Savior Jesus Christ
questions.correctAnswer: The blessed hope and coming of the glory of the great God and our Savior Jesus Christ
questions.explanation: "Looking for the blessed hope and coming of the glory of the great God and our Saviour Jesus Christ."

questions.prompt: "Violet or purple is used in Advent and ____."
questions.explanation: The General Instruction of the Roman Missal names Advent and Lent as the seasons of violet or purple.

citations.reference: General Instruction of the Roman Missal 346

questions.prompt: True or False: According to the Catechism, in celebrating the liturgy of Advent the Church shares in the long preparation for the Savior's first coming.
questions.explanation: "By sharing in the long preparation for the Saviour's first coming, the faithful renew their ardent desire for his second coming."

questions.prompt: According to the Directory on Popular Piety, what does the progressive lighting of the Advent wreath's candles recall?
choices: The twelve apostles who went out to the nations of the earth
The days of the Maccabean revolt and the rededication of the Temple
The various stages of salvation history prior to Christ's coming
The four Gospels and the four rivers of the garden of Eden
questions.correctAnswer: The various stages of salvation history prior to Christ's coming
questions.explanation: The wreath "is a recollection of the various stages of salvation history prior to Christ's coming and a symbol of the prophetic light gradually illuminating the long night prior to the rising of the Sun of justice."

citations.reference: Directory on Popular Piety and the Liturgy 98

questions.prompt: True or False: The Directory describes the Advent wreath as a symbol of the prophetic light gradually illuminating the long night before the rising of the Sun of justice.
questions.explanation: That is how the Directory on Popular Piety and the Liturgy describes it.

citations.reference: Directory on Popular Piety and the Liturgy 98

questions.prompt: How many candles does the Advent wreath have, lit "Sunday after Sunday until the Solemnity of Christmas"?
questions.explanation: "The Advent wreath, with the progressive lighting of its four candles, Sunday after Sunday, until the Solemnity of Christmas."

citations.reference: Directory on Popular Piety and the Liturgy 98

questions.prompt: In the Hispanic and Latin American tradition, what do the posadas represent?
choices: The journey to Bethlehem of Joseph and Mary and their search for a place in which Jesus would be born
The visit of the Magi to Bethlehem and their journey home by another way
The flight into Egypt of Joseph and Mary and their return after the death of Herod
The visit of Mary to Elizabeth in the hill country of Judea and her return
questions.correctAnswer: The journey to Bethlehem of Joseph and Mary and their search for a place in which Jesus would be born
questions.explanation: Advent processions "represent the journey to Bethlehem of Joseph and Mary and their search for a place in which Jesus would be born (the posadas in the Hispanic and Latin American tradition)."

citations.reference: Directory on Popular Piety and the Liturgy 99

questions.prompt: The Jesse tree takes its name from the image in Isaias 11:1 of a rod coming forth out of the root of whom?
questions.explanation: "And there shall come forth a rod out of the root of Jesse, and a flower shall rise up out of his root."

questions.prompt: The Advent chant "Rorate caeli" ("Drop down dew, ye heavens") takes its opening words from which prophet?
questions.explanation: "Drop down dew, ye heavens, from above, and let the clouds rain the just" is Isaiah 45:8.

questions.prompt: True or False: The Directory says the Christmas novena began as a requirement of canon law.
questions.explanation: No: "The Christmas novena began as a means of communicating the riches of the Liturgy to the faithful who were unable easily to grasp it."

citations.reference: Directory on Popular Piety and the Liturgy 103

questions.prompt: Which words from Saint Paul, "Rejoice in the Lord always", give Gaudete Sunday its name?
questions.explanation: The third Sunday of Advent is named from the first word of its Introit, Gaudete ("Rejoice"), from Saint Paul's words to the Philippians: "Rejoice in the Lord always."

citations.reference: General Instruction of the Roman Missal 346

questions.prompt: True or False: According to the Catechism, Christians pray "Maranatha" in the Eucharist to delay Christ's return.
questions.explanation: No: Christians pray, above all in the Eucharist, "to hasten Christ's return by saying to him: Maranatha! 'Our Lord, come!'"

questions.prompt: How does the Catechism describe the present time, between the Ascension and the Lord's return?
choices: A time of rest, in which nothing more is asked of the Church
A time of waiting and watching
A time without trial, in which the kingdom is complete
A time of silence, in which the Spirit speaks no more
questions.correctAnswer: A time of waiting and watching
questions.explanation: "According to the Lord, the present time is the time of the Spirit and of witness ... It is a time of waiting and watching."

questions.prompt: True or False: According to the Catechism, only the Son knows the day and the hour of the Last Judgment.
questions.explanation: No: "Only the Father knows the day and the hour."

questions.prompt: According to Matthew 24:36, who knows that day and hour?
questions.explanation: "But of that day and hour no one knoweth, not the angels of heaven, but the Father alone."

questions.prompt: According to 1 Thessalonians 5:2, how shall the day of the Lord come?
choices: As a thief in the night
With the sound of a trumpet only
questions.correctAnswer: As a thief in the night
questions.explanation: "For yourselves know perfectly, that the day of the Lord shall so come, as a thief in the night."

questions.prompt: In Apocalypse 22:20, what is the response to "Surely I come quickly"?
choices: Blessed be the name of the Lord
questions.explanation: "Surely I come quickly: Amen. Come, Lord Jesus."

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, what will Christ achieve when he comes in glory on Judgment Day?
choices: The restoration of the earthly kingdom of Israel
The definitive triumph of good over evil
questions.correctAnswer: The definitive triumph of good over evil
questions.explanation: "On Judgement Day at the end of the world, Christ will come in glory to achieve the definitive triumph of good over evil."

questions.prompt: True or False: According to the Catechism, on the Last Day Jesus will say: "as you did it to one of the least of these my brethren, you did it to me."
questions.explanation: "On the Last Day Jesus will say: 'Truly I say to you, as you did it to one of the least of these my brethren, you did it to me.'"

questions.prompt: According to the Catechism, who is "the purest figure" among the holy women who kept alive the hope of Israel's salvation?
questions.explanation: Holy women such as Sarah, Rebecca, Rachel, Miriam, Deborah, Hannah, Judith and Esther "kept alive the hope of Israel's salvation. The purest figure among them is Mary."

questions.prompt: Which prophet says, "Behold a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and his name shall be called Emmanuel"?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:14, quoted by Saint Matthew.

questions.prompt: Which prophet names Bethlehem as the place from which the ruler in Israel will come forth?
questions.explanation: "And thou, Bethlehem Ephrata, art a little one among the thousands of Juda: out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be the ruler in Israel."

questions.prompt: Which prophet announces a new covenant "not according to the covenant which I made with their fathers"?
questions.explanation: "Behold the days shall come, saith the Lord, and I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel, and with the house of Juda."

questions.prompt: Which prophet tells the daughter of Zion that "the king of Israel the Lord is in the midst of thee"?
questions.explanation: "Give praise, O daughter of Sion ... the king of Israel the Lord is in the midst of thee, thou shalt fear evil no more."

questions.prompt: Which prophet says, "Behold I send my angel, and he shall prepare the way before my face"?
questions.explanation: "Behold I send my angel, and he shall prepare the way before my face. And presently the Lord, whom you seek ... shall come to his temple."

questions.prompt: True or False: According to the Catechism, two prophetic lines, one leading to the expectation of the Messiah and one announcing a new Spirit, converge in the small Remnant, the people of the poor.
questions.explanation: "They converge in the small Remnant, the people of the poor, who await in hope the 'consolation of Israel' and 'the redemption of Jerusalem.'"
